style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A post-exile hymn in three stanzas, each beginning with a call to praise, and each stanza turning on the same astonishment: the God who runs the cosmos is the God who tends the small. He builds Jerusalem and gathers her exiles -- and heals broken hearts, bandaging their wounds; then in the same breath He counts the stars and names each one, His understanding beyond any number. He covers the sky with clouds and grows grass on the mountains -- and feeds the raven chicks when they caw. And His pleasure is not in cavalry or infantry but in those who fear Him and hope in His covenant love. The third stanza is winter in Judea: snow like wool, frost like ash, ice flung down like crumbs, and then the thaw -- and every one of these is His word running to the earth and doing what it says. The last turn is the sharpest: the same word that commands the snow was declared to Jacob as statutes; no other nation got that, and the psalm ends not in boasting but in hallelujah.

1.text: Praise the LORD! For it is good to make music to our God; it is delightful, and praise is fitting.
1.amp: Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah]: for it is good [tov] to sing praises [zamar] unto our God [Elohim]; for it is pleasant [naim -- delightful]; and praise [tehillah] is comely [naveh -- fitting, becoming].
1.notes: Three adjectives for praise: tov, naim, naveh (H2896, H5273, H5000) -- good, delightful, becoming. Right, enjoyable, and fitting: making music (zamar, H2167) is not only duty but pleasure, and not only pleasure but propriety -- the one activity that suits a creature perfectly.

2.text: The LORD builds Jerusalem up; He gathers in the scattered exiles of Israel.
2.amp: The LORD [YHWH] does build up [banah] Jerusalem [Yerushalaim]: He gathers together [kanas] the outcasts [dachah -- the driven-out, the scattered] of Israel [Yisrael].
2.notes: A post-exile psalm: banah (H1129) Jerusalem -- Nehemiah's walls going up -- and kanas nidche Yisrael (H3664, H1760, H3478), the gathering of those who had been shoved out. The rebuilt city and the regathered people are the LORD's own construction project.

3.text: He heals the broken-hearted and bandages their wounds.
3.amp: He heals [rapha] the broken [shabar -- shattered] in heart [leb], and binds up [chabash -- bandages] their wounds ['griefs', atstsebet, the KJV margin].
3.notes: Between the city-building and the star-counting stands the field hospital: rapha (H7495), healing, for shebure leb (H7665, H3820), the shattered of heart -- exiles are not only relocated but mended. chabash (H2280) is the bandaging verb: God with His hands full of linen, dressing atstsebot (H6094), the griefs that are wounds.

4.text: He counts the number of the stars; He calls each one of them by name.
4.amp: He tells [manah -- counts, assigns] the number [mispar] of the stars [kokab]; He calls [qara] them all by their names [shem].
4.notes: The zoom-out that makes verse 3 breathtaking: the same Physician manah (H4487) the kokabim (H3556) -- a census of the galaxies -- and qara shemot (H7121, H8034), names each one. The God who tracks every star is not going to lose track of one broken heart (cf. Isaiah 40:26-27).

5.text: Great is our Lord, and vast in power; His understanding is beyond all number.
5.amp: Great [gadol] is our Lord [Adon], and of great [rav] power [koach]: His understanding [tebunah] is infinite [mispar -- 'of his understanding there is no number', the KJV margin].
5.notes: Adonenu gadol ve-rav koach (H113, H1419, H7227, H3581) -- and the margin's literal: li-tebunato en mispar (H8394, H4557), His understanding has no number. The stars had a mispar (v. 4); His comprehension does not. Isaiah 40:28's 'no searching of his understanding', put in arithmetic terms.

6.text: The LORD lifts the humble up; He brings the wicked down to the ground.
6.amp: The LORD [YHWH] lifts up [ud -- restores, sets upright] the meek [anav -- the humble, the afflicted]: He casts [shaphel -- brings low] the wicked [rasha] down to the ground [eretz].
6.notes: The reversal-verse: ud anavim (H5749, H6035) -- the lowly lifted and held up -- and mashpil reshaim (H8213, H7563) ade-eretz (H776), the wicked lowered to the dirt. The infinite understanding of verse 5 is not neutral; it takes sides.

7.text: Answer the LORD with a song of thanksgiving; make music on the lyre to our God,
7.amp: Sing [anah -- answer, sing responsively] unto the LORD [YHWH] with thanksgiving [todah]; sing praise [zamar] upon the harp [kinnor -- lyre] unto our God [Elohim]:
7.notes: enu la-YHWH (H6030): the verb is 'answer' -- responsive song, one side calling and the other replying, be-todah (H8426), with thanksgiving. The kinnor (H3658), the lyre, joins for the second stanza, which sings the God of weather and ravens.

8.text: who covers the sky with clouds, who readies rain for the earth, who makes grass sprout on the mountains.
8.amp: Who covers [kasah] the heaven [shamayim] with clouds [ab], who prepares [kun] rain [matar] for the earth [eretz], who makes grass [chatsir] to grow [tsamach -- sprout] upon the mountains [har].
8.notes: Three participles of providence: kasah shamayim be-abim (H3680, H8064, H5645), kun matar (H3559, H4306), tsamach chatsir (H6779, H2682) on the harim (H2022), the mountains -- clouds, rain, grass, the whole water cycle credited to a Person. Weather as an ongoing verb of God.

9.text: He gives the animals their food, and the young ravens what they cry for.
9.amp: He gives [natan] to the beast [behemah] his food [lechem]; and to the young [ben] ravens [oreb] which cry [qara].
9.notes: natan lechem li-behemah (H5414, H3899, H929) -- and to the bene oreb (H1121, H6158), the raven chicks, unclean birds whose parents were thought to abandon them. Their qara (H7121), their caw, counted as a prayer God answers (cf. Job 38:41; Luke 12:24).

10.text: He takes no delight in the horse's strength; He takes no pleasure in a man's powerful legs.
10.amp: He delights [chaphets] not in the strength [geburah] of the horse [sus]: He takes not pleasure [ratsah] in the legs [shoq] of a man [ish].
10.notes: The two military assets of the ancient world -- geburat ha-sus (H1369, H5483), cavalry, and shoqe ha-ish (H7785, H376), infantry legs that can march and run -- and God is unimpressed by both: lo yechpats, lo yirtseh (H2654, H7521). The Counter of stars does not scout for muscle.

11.text: The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear Him, in those who wait in hope for His covenant love.
11.amp: The LORD [YHWH] takes pleasure [ratsah] in them that fear [yare] Him, in those that hope [yachal -- wait expectantly] in His mercy [chesed -- covenant love].
11.notes: What DOES please Him: ratsah (H7521) -- the same pleasure-verb withheld from the runner's legs in verse 10 -- in the yereim and the meyachalim le-chasdo (H3373, H3176, H2617): reverence and hope. Not the strong but the fearing-and-hoping are God's delight; the disqualification of verse 10 becomes the invitation of verse 11.

12.text: Extol the LORD, O Jerusalem! Sing the praise of your God, O Zion!
12.amp: Praise [shabach -- laud, extol] the LORD [YHWH], O Jerusalem [Yerushalaim]; praise [halal] your God [Elohim], O Zion [Tsiyyon].
12.notes: The third stanza's call, addressed to the city itself: shabach and halal (H7623, H1984) -- Yerushalaim and Tsiyyon (H6726) commanded to praise Elohayikh, YOUR God. The rebuilt walls of verse 2 now have inhabitants who sing.

13.text: For He has made the bars of your gates strong; He has blessed your children within your walls.
13.amp: For He has strengthened [chazaq] the bars [beriach -- bolts] of your gates [shaar]; He has blessed [barak] your children [ben] within [qereb] you.
13.notes: chizzaq beriche shearayikh (H2388, H1280, H8179): Nehemiah 7:3's bolted gates, but credited to God's hand -- security as grace. And barak banayikh be-qirbekh (H1288, H1121, H7130): the blessing is on the people inside the walls, not the masonry.

14.text: He makes peace within your borders; He satisfies you with the finest of the wheat.
14.amp: He makes ['who maketh thy border peace', sum shalom, the KJV margin] peace [shalom] in your borders [gebul], and fills [saba -- satisfies] you with the finest ['fat', chelev, the KJV margin] of the wheat [chittah].
14.notes: shalom on the gebul (H7965, H1366) -- quiet frontiers -- and saba (H7646), satisfying you, with chelev chittim (H2459, H2406), literally 'the fat of wheat', the richest kernels of the crop (cf. Deuteronomy 32:14; Psalm 81:16). Peace outside, plenty inside: the covenant's twin blessings.

15.text: He sends His command out to the earth; His word runs very swiftly.
15.amp: He sends forth [shalach] His commandment [imrah -- His utterance] upon earth [eretz]: His word [dabar] runs [ruts] very swiftly [meherah].
15.notes: shalach imrato (H7971, H565) -- God's utterance dispatched like a courier -- and ad-meherah yaruts debaro (H4120, H7323, H1697): the word runs, at speed. The winter stanza that follows is what the running word does when it arrives.

16.text: He lays down snow like wool; He scatters the frost like ash.
16.amp: He gives [natan] snow [sheleg] like wool [tsemer]: He scatters [pazar] the hoarfrost [kephor] like ashes [epher].
16.notes: Two similes from a Judean winter: sheleg ka-tsamer (H7950, H6785), snow laid down like a fleece; kephor ka-epher (H3713, H665), frost scattered (pazar, H6340) like ash. Nothing in the weather happens without a giving and a scattering hand.

17.text: He hurls His ice down like crumbs -- before His cold, who can stand?
17.amp: He casts forth [shalak -- hurls] His ice [qerach] like morsels [path -- crumbs, fragments]: who can stand [amad] before [panim] His cold [qarah]?
17.notes: mashlikh qarcho ke-phittim (H7993, H7140, H6595): hail flung down like bread-crumbs from a table -- casual for Him, dangerous for us. liphne qarato mi yaamod (H7135, H5975): the same 'who can stand' asked elsewhere of His wrath, here asked of His frost.

18.text: He sends out His word and melts them; He lets His wind breathe over them, and the waters run freely.
18.amp: He sends out [shalach] His word [dabar], and melts [masah] them: He causes His wind [ruach] to blow [nashab], and the waters [mayim] flow [nazal -- trickle, run].
18.notes: The thaw is as much a word as the freeze: yishlach debaro (H7971, H1697), He sends His word, and the ice masah (H4529), melts; ruach (H7307), the wind, blows and mayim nazal (H4325, H5140), the waters flow. Spring is a second command, not a natural recovery from the first.

19.text: He makes His word known to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments known to Israel.
19.amp: He shows [nagad -- declares] His word ['his words', dabar, the KJV margin] unto Jacob [Yaaqob], His statutes [choq] and His judgments [mishpat] unto Israel [Yisrael].
19.notes: The word that runs to the earth (v. 15) and melts the ice (v. 18) is the same dabar (H1697) that was declared (nagad, H5046) to Yaaqob (H3290) as chuqqim and mishpatim (H2706, H4941), statutes and judgments. Snow obeys it automatically; Israel was given it to obey on purpose.

20.text: He has not done this for any other nation; as for His judgments, they have not known them. Praise the LORD!
20.amp: He has not dealt [asah] so with any nation [goy]: and as for His judgments [mishpat], they have not known [yada] them. Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah].
20.notes: The privilege stated without boast: lo asah khen le-khol goy (H6213, H1471) -- no other nation received the mishpatim (H4941), and bal yedaum (H3045), they do not know them. A responsibility more than a rank (cf. Deuteronomy 4:7-8; Romans 3:1-2); and the Hallelujah closes it.
